Key inquiry question: Why do we match tactile representations of circuit symbols with their respective names?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Tactile Representations of Circuit Symbols • Fuse • Capacitor • Variable resistors • Potential dividers • Galvanometer together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: the learner tactually explores tactile representations of circuit symbols and

assigns them their respective names.

• Communication and Collaboration: the learner shares findings with peers after tactually exploring tactile

representations of circuit symbols.

Values:
● Love: the learner shares the available learning resources with peers when tactually exploring the tactile representations

of circuit symbols and assigning them their respective real circuit apparatus.

● Social justice: the learner inspires solidarity with others when working in groups to tactually explore tactile

representations of circuit symbols and note their shape and the accompanying Braille letters

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety and security: the learner handles real circuit symbols with care to avoid breakages.
